blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as a plain function a reader can follow without the plan: a named constant for the premium threshold (e.g. `PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`) with a comparison `price.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS` instead of `(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8`, two explicit arrays (or a `{ cheap, premium }` result type instead of `Record<string, Price[]>` with "hi"/"lo" keys), a simple loop instead of the comma-expression reducer with `||=`, and descriptive names instead of `ps`, `a`, `p`. A newcomer reading the doc comment "Splits prices into the cheap and the premium ones" cannot tell from line 10 where "premium" starts: `>> 4` divides by 16 and the mask `0x3e8` (1000) tests scattered bits rather than a threshold, so they will likely read it as "cents above some value" when it is not a monotonic comparison (e.g. 16000 cents gives 1000 & 1000 → "hi", but 16384 cents gives 1024 & 1000 = 0 → "lo"). The developer should confirm the intended rule; the readable version makes it visible. Also a bucket key is missing entirely when no price falls in it, which the `Record<string, …>` type does not tell the caller.
findings.title: `bucket` hides its premium threshold in a bit-twiddling one-liner
